The '''Isatabith rain forest''',<ref name="Lost Stars" /> also known as the '''Isatabith forest''', was located on the [[Core Worlds|Core World]]<ref name="Encyclopedia">{{EncyclopediaCite|Core Worlds, Colonies, the Inner Rim and Expansion Region}}</ref> of [[Alderaan]]<ref name="Lost Stars" /> and partially shared its name with [[Isatabith falls]].<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> The [[Water|rain]] [[forest]] was one of multiple Alderaanian locations that were described to [[Galactic Empire|Imperial]] [[pilot]] [[Thane Kyrell]] by his friend [[Nash Windrider]] during the latter's efforts to extol the [[planet]]'s natural beauty and list its best places to visit,<ref name="Lost Stars" /> with the location featuring ample [[Plant|vegetation]] and [[bird]]s.<ref name="Galactic Atlas" />

Kyrell later thought of both the rain forest and the [[Cloudshape Falls]] as potential destinations for he and his friend just before witnessing the [[Destruction of Alderaan|destruction]] of Alderaan<ref name="Lost Stars" /> in [[1 BBY]], where the forest was destroyed as well.<ref name="Date" /> An illustration of the Isatabith rain forest was included a [[map]] of Alderaan made by the [[artist]] [[Gammit Chond]], which was included in an updated version of the ''[[Galactic Atlas]]'' [[book]] published by the [[Graf Archive]] at some point no earlier than [[35 ABY]].<ref name="Galactic Atlas" />

==Behind the scenes==
The Isatabith rain forest was first mentioned in the [[2015]] novel ''[[Lost Stars]]'', written by [[Claudia Gray]].<ref name="Lost Stars" /> It was first identified as the Isatabith forest in  "[[Core Worlds, Colonies, the Inner Rim and Expansion Region]]," a part of De Agostini's [[Star Wars Encyclopedia (series)|''Star Wars Encyclopedia'']] line<ref name="Encyclopedia" /> that was released on [[June 8]], [[2022]].<ref name="Altaya">{{Altaya|url=livres-bd/encyclopedie-star-wars|text=Encyclopédie Star Wars}}</ref> The forest was first pictured in the [[2025]] reference book ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Atlas: Updated Edition]]'', written by [[Emil Fortune]] and [[Paddy Kempshall]] and illustrated by [[Tim McDonagh]].<ref name="Galactic Atlas" />
